answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because island only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, vertex is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any echo approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
